title: Simultaneous semi-dry electrophoretic transfer of a wide range of differently sized proteins for immunoblotting.
protocol: Clean glass plates with 70 % ethanol.
Follow cleaning with acetone for easy gel removal later.
Assemble the glass plates using spacers.
Secure the assembly with bull clips on each side.
Heat 1 % agarose in microwave to liquefy.
Seal the gel plate assembly with 1 % agarose.
Pipette small amounts of 1 % agarose between the plates, holding at a steep angle so it flows along the spacer towards the bottom.
Reverse the angle of the gel once agarose reaches the bottom.
Add more agarose in-between the plates while maintaining reverse angle to flow along the other spacer.
Swap the angle of the gel again once agarose covers as much of the bottom part as possible.
Place a magnetic stir plate on an elevated surface, about 30 cm higher than where assembled gel plates stand.
Position the gradient maker on the magnetic stir plate.
Add magnetic stir bars to mixing chambers in the gradient maker.
Ensure valves are closed before dispensing premix solution into the gradient maker.
For large gels, pipette 20 ml of 4 % and 20 ml of 17 % acrylamide premix into left and right mixing chambers respectively.
Add 200 µl of 10 % APS to each chamber.
Add 20 µl of TEMED to each chamber.
Pipette 6 ml of acrylamide premix into each chamber.
Add 60 μl of 10% APS to each chamber.
Add 6 μl of TEMED to each chamber.
Allow the solutions to mix for only a few seconds.
Open the valve between the mixing chambers.
Open the outside valve.
Trigger flow by gently squeezing the delivery tube if necessary.
Place the tubing near the top centre of the tall plate as soon as liquid begins to flow.
Allow the solution to run down the plate to avoid inclusion of air pockets in the gel.
Insert a comb into the setup.
Add dH2O to the chambers of the gradient former and allow it to exit through the tube.
Repeat the addition of water until all necessary steps are completed.
Let the gel polymerize for about 1 hour or longer if APS is not fresh.
Carefully remove the comb and the bottom spacer.
Rinse the wells with dH2O to remove excess acrylamide.
Remove excess liquid from the wells.
Add running buffer to the bottom reservoir of the electrophoresis unit.
Wipe the surface of the reservoir with a paper towel to remove air bubbles.
Place one bottom corner of the gel in the buffer and slowly lower the other corner to allow air bubbles to escape.
Check that the bottom of the gel is completely submerged in the buffer.
Clamp the gel in place with bull clips.
Fill the top reservoir with running buffer until the wells are just covered.
Rinse the wells with running buffer prior to loading protein samples.
Run the large gel at 250 V; 100 mA, and the small gel at 100-150 V until the dye front is near the bottom of the gel.
Disassemble the plates carefully.
Remove the agarose and other excess parts of the gel.
Equilibrate the gel in cold transfer buffer for a few minutes to remove SDS and potential gel fragments.
Submerge the membrane in 100% methanol for 15 seconds.
Soak the membrane in cold transfer buffer for a few minutes with gentle shaking.
Pre-wet a triple layer of 3MM filter paper in cold transfer buffer by submerging one side first and then slowly lowering it into the buffer.
Place the pre-soaked 3MM filter paper stack on the clean bench.
Align the pre-soaked membrane on top of the wet filter papers.
Remove excess buffer and trapped air bubbles from the membrane using a blot roller or pipette.
Place the soaked gel on top of the membrane.
Remove air bubbles from between the gel and membrane with a blot roller, pipette, or gloved hands.
Add three sheets of pre-wetted 3MM filter paper onto the gel.
Gently remove air bubbles from the entire sandwich assembly.
Transfer the assembled sandwich to the semi-dry transfer unit.
Carefully lower the sandwich onto a small puddle of transfer buffer on the bottom electrode (anode).
Remove excess buffer from around the electrodes using dry paper towels.
Place the upper electrode (cathode) on top of the anode plate.
Transfer for 45 minutes at 25V, 1A.
Check the voltage current status at the very beginning of transfer.
Wash the membrane in TBS-T after transfer is completed.
Disassemble the unit after completing the transfer.
Stain the membrane in Ponceau solution for 10 minutes to check efficiency of transfer.
Rinse the membrane with 1% v/v acetic acid until protein bands are clearly visible.
Document the result using a document scanner or camera.
Incubate the membrane for a few minutes in TBS-T.
